findings.source_quote: καὶ σεαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ἐνεδρεύσεις
findings.english_quote: you will ensnare both yourself and your hearers.
findings.issue: The general sense of endangering both parties is conveyed, but “ensnare” substitutes a trapping image for the more specific ambush image of ἐνεδρεύσεις.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “you will lay an ambush for both yourself and your hearers.” Preserve the ambush image in the revised wording and review that replacement afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἐξασκήσατε τὴν χριστοῦ νύμφην εἰς σωφροσύνην
findings.issue: The standalone christological designation is rendered “Christ” without discussing whether it functions titularly here. In this bridal context, “the Messiah’s bride” is the source-transparent candidate required by the supplied policy; no name-like exception is documented.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “train the Messiah’s bride in chastity.” Use that wording if χριστοῦ is understood titularly, or document contextual evidence for retaining a name-like “Christ.”

findings.source_quote: ὑμεῖς δὲ δίκην δώσετε μήπως παρὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀμέλειαν γέγονεν ἡ ἁμαρτία
findings.english_quote: and you will pay the penalty if perhaps the sin came about through your neglect.
findings.issue: The Greek explicitly asserts δίκην δώσετε and then attaches the difficult μήπως clause. The draft makes payment of the penalty conditional on negligence. That conditional restriction is an interpretive construction, not an unambiguously expressed Greek condition, and its uncertainty is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Do not finalize the conditional restriction without examining parallels for δίκην διδόναι with μήπως. Preserve the explicit penalty statement and add a note explaining the uncertain dependency and force of μήπως, including the possible “whether/lest perhaps” senses and the rationale for any retained conditional interpretation. This is a meaning problem, not evidence of transcription corruption.

findings.source_quote: σπουδάζετε πυκνότερον συνέστιοι ἀλλήλων γίνεσθαι ὡς δύνασθε
findings.english_quote: make every effort to dine with one another as often as you can
findings.issue: The draft merges the comparative πυκνότερον and the qualification ὡς δύνασθε into a maximum-frequency expression. The Greek expressly calls for greater frequency, qualified by ability. The lexical note recognizes increased frequency, but the main text does not preserve it distinctly.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “make every effort to dine with one another more frequently, as you are able.” Review the revised wording before accepting it.

findings.source_quote: πᾶν καλὸν ἡ φιλανθρωπία ὑμᾶς ποιεῖν διδάξει, ὥσπερ ἡ μισανθρωπία τοῖς μὴ βουλομένοις σώζεσθαι τὴν κακοπραξίαν ὑποδείκνυσιν
findings.english_quote: benevolence will teach you to do every good thing, just as misanthropy points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved.
findings.issue: The direct φιλανθρωπία/μισανθρωπία antithesis shares an explicit human referent. “Benevolence” beside the technical English “misanthropy” makes that wording pattern less visible and is less accessible than available source-transparent alternatives.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare “love of humanity … hatred of humanity” or “human kindness … hatred of humanity.” Preserve both the human referent and the contrast. If changing the φιλανθρωπία rendering, review its cognate renderings in section 8 for consistency or document the contextual exception.

findings.source_quote: ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;
findings.english_quote: Do you carefully observe fair balances, measures, weights, and the just standards of the various localities?
findings.issue: The draft treats τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια as a separate fourth item and introduces “and.” The phrase can instead identify the preceding balances, measures, and weights as the locally lawful or correct ones. That syntactic uncertainty is not disclosed. The supplied question punctuation itself is properly preserved and should not be corrected merely because the surrounding instructions favor an imperative reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare an appositional rendering such as “Do you carefully observe balances, measures, and weights—the lawful standards of the localities?” Disclose the alternative interpretation as a separate reference to local legal requirements. Retain the supplied question punctuation and keep the disclosed word-division feature τῶντόπων distinct from this interpretive issue.

findings.source_quote: ἐκ θεοῦ δικαίου, τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ
findings.english_quote: from the righteous God—who only for now is patient and good—
findings.issue: “Only for now” places an exclusive temporal limit on God's patience and goodness. The supplied μόνου is a genitive adjective agreeing with God, not the adverb μόνον modifying νῦν. The note preserves “God alone” as an alternative but does not justify promoting the temporally restrictive interpretation to the main text.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “from the righteous God—who alone is now patient and good—.” Remove the unsupported “only for now” limitation. If another interpretation of the adjective's scope is proposed, document its grammatical basis without correcting μόνου or importing another edition's wording. Review any replacement afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα οἱ ἀγαθοὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα
findings.english_quote: so that the good may thereafter enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners will, as evil people, receive inexpressible punishment throughout the age?
findings.issue: The source changes from ἀιδίως to the temporal accusative τὸν αἰῶνα, but a change of expression does not itself establish a contrast in duration. “Throughout the age” can suggest a bounded epoch beside “everlastingly.” The note acknowledges the idiomatic “forever” sense but supplies no contextual justification for the duration-sounding distinction adopted in the main text.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare “everlastingly … forever,” preserving the different Greek expressions and the literal “for the age” in a note. If “throughout the age” is retained, explain that no finite endpoint is being asserted and preserve the idiomatic alternative without deriving different durations from morphology alone. Review the resulting main text and note together before acceptance.
